question.prompt: Medians \(AD\) and \(CE\) of triangle \(ABC\) intersect in \(M.\) The midpoint of \(AE\) is \(N.\) Let the area of triangle \(MNE\) be \(k\) times the area of triangle \(ABC.\) Then \(k\) equals:

solutions.explanation:
Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of triangle \(XYZ\). Because \(CE\) is a median, \(E\) is the midpoint of \(AB\), so triangles \(ACE\) and \(ABC\) have the same altitude from \(C\) and bases in the ratio \(1:2\). Hence
\[
[ACE]=\frac12[ABC].
\]
The intersection of the medians is the centroid, which divides each median in the ratio \(2:1\) from the vertex. Thus \(CM:ME=2:1\), giving \(ME=CE/3\). Triangles \(AME\) and \(ACE\) have bases on the same line \(CE\) and the same altitude from \(A\), so
\[
[AME]=\frac13[ACE]=\frac16[ABC].
\]
Finally, \(N\) is the midpoint of \(AE\). Triangles \(MNE\) and \(MAE\) share the altitude from \(M\) to \(AB\), while \(NE=AE/2\). Therefore
\[
[MNE]=\frac12[MAE]=\frac1{12}[ABC].
\]
Thus \(\boxed{k=\frac1{12}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Use the centroid ratio

solutions.explanation:
Write \([XYZ]\) for triangle area and let \(S=[ABC]\). Join \(B\) to \(M\). Since \(AD\) is a median,
\[
[ABD]=[ACD]=\frac S2.
\]
Also, \([BMD]=[CMD]\): their bases \(BD\) and \(DC\) are equal, and they share the altitude from \(M\) to \(BC\). Subtracting these equal small areas from the equal half-triangle areas gives \([ABM]=[ACM]\). Call this common area \(t\).

Because \(E\) is the midpoint of \(AB\), triangles \(AME\) and \(BME\) each have area \(t/2\). Median \(CE\) also halves the original triangle's area, so
\[
\frac S2=[ACE]=[ACM]+[AME]
=t+\frac t2.
\]
Thus \(t=S/3\) and \([AME]=S/6\). Since \(N\) is the midpoint of \(AE\), triangles \(MNE\) and \(MAE\) have the same altitude and bases in the ratio \(1:2\). Consequently,
\[
[MNE]=\frac12[MAE]=\frac S{12}.
\]
Therefore \(\boxed{k=\frac1{12}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Use only the equal areas made by medians
